item.title: Friday Favorites 34
item.description:
Happy Friday,

Cue the music, brew that pot. I had a productive week of owling: a great horned, two barred, a northern saw-whet, and TWO long-eared owls (firsts for me) swooped over me a dozen times the day before the full moon. Unreal!

Here are 10 interesting things worth sharing this week:

  1. Chat Pile is loud, sludgy band with songs about American ugliness, and they ripped on their recent KEXP set, mostly thanks to singer Raygun Busch’s performance. I read a spot-on Instagram comment that Raygun brings mad toddler energy (in a good way!) to his shows, complete with not wearing shoes or a shirt when onstage.
  2. As an avid Field Notes daily user since 2019, I’m stoked the gang brought back a pocket planner just in time for the new year. (I loved their Ignition series from 2021.)
  3. New Field Notes has me daydreaming about ordering a bulk, custom order of the iconic Bic Clic Stic pens you used to see in restaurants and businesses when you were a kid (now Bic is calling them “retro pens?”). While you noodle on what to put on your custom order, read this ode to the iconic pen.
  4. Bob Dylan’s “Self Portrait” is one of his weirder albums with very different sounds. I didn’t know Mumford’s “The Boxer” was a cover from it! “Being a Bob fan feels like being in on an inside joke that you’re actually not in on, but you can pretend to be in on.”
  5. Anything related to wellness or productivity has gotten shoveled into “should” and “to-do” land for me. Most of it feels like I can never do enough of it or do it the right way for it to be “right.” So this article about how optimization has ruined wellness was thought-provoking. (I want Jia Tolentino to write a cultural essay about this please.)
  6. Love scanning through Big Book Roundups and waiting for people to disagree about what was and wasn’t included.
  7. Louis L’Amour wrote a great memoir about reading, writing, and traveling — so I’ve really enjoyed his son Beau making videos about him, his books, and what he’s learned about writing.
  8. “You may just need to learn how to really try hard!”
  9. A few times a year a big publication will write about how typewriters are still useful, and I read them every time. Pretty cool how these products are 50-100 years old, still work as they were meant, and keep getting passed from new owner to new owner.
  10. Everyone’s talking about GTAVI, but I don’t have a PS5, so I’m mostly thinking about how they managed to get SO MANY musicians to collab on its game soundtrack.

See you on down the dusty trail,
